timeQualification: The paper defines JD 2455305.0 as asterocentric (light-time-corrected), without naming UTC/TT/TDB. This preparation treats that numerical epoch as TT; a clock-scale ambiguity up to 70 seconds contributes less than 0.41 degree of phase, separate from the much larger source-parameter/extrapolation uncertainty. No light-time correction is applied to the resulting geometric vector.

parameterConversion: The orbital normal gives i = 90 − poleLatitude and Ω = poleLongitude + 90 modulo 360. The circular fit uses ω = 0 as an element convention and M0 = L0 − Ω; this preserves the published longitude, rather than inventing a pericenter phase.
modelQualification: Section 2.2 sets eccentricity to zero for the all-apparition drift fit. Preserve constant mean separation in this display model; the approximately 1.2 cm/year physical radius drift is negligible relative to the ±15 m source scale uncertainty. The quadratic anomaly coefficient is half the mean-motion derivative, so it enters M directly with no extra factor of 1/2.

uncertainties.note: Individual fit ranges are not a full covariance matrix. The pole uncertainty area is not a rectangular RA/Dec error box.
